title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Compiling a project with a [MessagePackObject] type that has a member typed as a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly (for example ValueTuple-like or a library GenericStruct<int>) does not make the source generator throw an IndexOutOfRangeException.
The same holds when the referenced generic value type is a record struct.
No CS8785 generator-failed warning or error is reported for these member types.
expectedTests: A generator test compiles a referenced assembly that defines a generic struct, then a consuming project with a [MessagePackObject] member of a closed form of that struct, and asserts the generator produced no exceptions or failure diagnostics.
The same test with a generic record struct from the referenced assembly.

expectedBehaviours: Running the MessagePack analyzers on a [MessagePackObject] type whose member is a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly does not throw IndexOutOfRangeException.
No AD0001 analyzer-crashed diagnostic is reported for that code.
Analyzer diagnostics that apply to the type are still reported as normal, and no spurious ones appear.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a closed generic struct member from a referenced metadata assembly checks that no AD0001 and no unexpected MsgPack diagnostics are produced.

expectedBehaviours: The consuming assembly gets a generated resolver and a formatter for the [MessagePackObject] type, as it does when the generic struct is declared in the same project.
At runtime, the generated resolver serializes and deserializes the object with the cross-assembly generic struct member without error.
expectedTests: A snapshot test checks the generated resolver and formatter output for a type with a member of a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly.
A round-trip test serializes and deserializes an instance through the generated resolver and checks the member value survives.

expectedBehaviours: If the generator or analyzer hits an unexpected condition with these types, the build shows it clearly as a failure or an error-level diagnostic, not only as a CS8785 or AD0001 warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver.
A successful build is never missing the expected generated resolver.
expectedTests: Generator tests fail when the generator reports exceptions or generator-failure diagnostics, so a silent warning cannot pass.

expectedBehaviours: Generated output for members of generic classes, non-generic structs and generic types declared in the same project matches the existing snapshot files with no changes.

story.what: TypeCollector now wraps the analyzer's diagnostic callback. Any diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation is dropped. Two member-diagnostic sites no longer index DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0], which is empty for metadata-only symbols. They use FirstOrDefault-based lookups that return a null location instead. The analyzer also stops running TypeCollector from [MessagePackObject] structs and only starts from classes and union interfaces. New tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata image and check that a consuming project builds with no diagnostics and gets its resolver. Docs are added to README.md and MsgPack004.md.
story.why: Requirement MP-2283: a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly, used as a member type, made the generator and analyzer throw IndexOutOfRangeException. Indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] fails for a metadata symbol with no syntax. The crash showed up only as CS8785 or AD0001 warnings, and the consuming assembly was left without a generated resolver.

findings.title: Analyzer no longer analyzes [MessagePackObject] structs declared in project
findings.detail: h3 removes TypeKind.Struct from the AnalyzeSymbol switch, so TypeCollector.Collect is never run with a project struct as the root symbol. All analyzer diagnostics for [MessagePackObject] structs (MsgPack004 missing keys, MsgPack005 key conflicts, MsgPack007 constructor mismatches, and others) silently disappear. The TypeCollector constructor still accepts structs (line 256), so this is inconsistent. It violates N2 (behaviour for non-generic structs and same-project types must not change), and the requirement does not ask for it. No test shows the struct analyzer diagnostics still work.

findings.title: Location-less diagnostics about project types are now silently dropped
findings.detail: Every analyzer diagnostic now goes through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. The filter drops anything whose location is not in source, including Location.None. Several diagnostics about the project's own types compute their location with null-propagating lookups. One example is CollidingMemberNamesInForceMapMode, whose location comes from the colliding symbol and is null when that symbol is from a referenced base class. Before, these were still reported (at no location). Now they vanish, so real errors in the consuming project can pass silently. This goes against N1 and N2.

citations.quote: this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null ? null : diagnostic => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, diagnostic);

findings.title: Generated resolver content for cross-assembly generic struct not verified
findings.detail: F3 requires the consuming assembly to get its resolver and a formatter registration, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project. The new tests set SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck and only check that a file with the resolver's hint name exists. A resolver that omits the GenericSerializationInfo for MyGenericStruct<int> or Item<int> would still pass. No snapshot test compares the generated output.

findings.title: No runtime round-trip test through the generated resolver
findings.detail: F3 expects an object with a cross-assembly closed generic struct member to serialize and deserialize through the generated resolver. No test in the change runs the generated resolver or checks that the member value survives a round trip.

findings.title: Generator failures still surface only as CS8785 warnings
findings.detail: N1 asks that a generator or analyzer failure must not pass as a mere warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. The change fixes two specific indexing sites but adds no guard or error-level reporting around collection. Any other unexpected exception during TypeCollector.Collect still becomes a CS8785 or AD0001 warning, and the build succeeds without a resolver.

findings.title: No test that same-project struct diagnostics are unchanged
findings.detail: N2 requires unchanged analyzer behaviour for structs and same-project types. The change alters which root symbols are analyzed and filters diagnostics, but adds no test that a [MessagePackObject] struct in the project still reports, for example, MsgPack004 for an unkeyed member.
